fix: none until GitHub announces Ed448 or ML-DSA signing keys
reason: GitHub verifies SSH commit signatures only for the key types it supports; Ed448 and ML-DSA are not among them, and no support is announced.
what: Commit signing with SSH keys uses Ed25519, not Ed448 + ML-DSA-87.

fix: none until a browser ships a stronger hybrid group
reason: X25519MLKEM768 is the strongest hybrid group browsers offer; no browser has announced X448 or ML-KEM-1024 groups.
what: Browser-facing TLS key exchange uses X25519MLKEM768, not X448 + ML-KEM-1024.

fix: none until browsers ship them; recheck at review
reason: WebCrypto ships neither Ed448 nor ML-KEM in every browser. Draft proposals exist but nothing has shipped across browsers.
what: In-browser cryptography through WebCrypto cannot use Ed448, X448, ML-DSA, ML-KEM or SHA-3. It uses, per operation: Ed25519 signatures (ECDSA P-384 with SHA-384 where a browser lacks Ed25519); X25519 key agreement (ECDH P-384 where a browser lacks X25519); AES-256-GCM; SHA-512; HMAC-SHA-512; HKDF-SHA-512. Anything weaker in the browser is a departure.

fix: none until a public CA and browsers support them
reason: No public CA issues Ed448 or ML-DSA certificates and browsers would not accept them. Cloudflare-managed edge certificates offer no ECDSA curve above P-256.
what: Public TLS certificates are ECDSA, not Ed448 + ML-DSA-87: P-384 wherever the issuing CA offers it (self-managed ACME, uploaded custom certificates); P-256 only on Cloudflare-managed edge certificates (Universal, Advanced, Total TLS), which Cloudflare issues on P-256 only.

reason: OpenSSH and GitHub offer no Ed448, ML-DSA or ML-KEM-1024; using them would lock us out of SSH, with no fix announced.
what: SSH host and user keys are Ed25519 (SSHFP type 4) with mlkem768x25519-sha256 key exchange, not Ed448 + ML-DSA-87 and X448 + ML-KEM-1024.

fix: none until a DKIM standard for stronger keys exists and receivers check it
reason: DKIM defines only RSA and Ed25519 (RFC 8463); there is no Ed448 DKIM standard, and many receivers still check only RSA, so mail would be rejected or marked spam.
what: Outbound mail is dual-signed DKIM Ed25519 + RSA-2048, an exception to no RSA.

fix: none until GitHub supports SHA-256 object format
reason: GitHub does not host SHA-256 repositories, and commit ids are what git and Actions pin to.
what: Git object ids, and the SHA pins on dependencies and workflow uses:, are SHA-1 commit hashes, not SHA3-512.

fix: none until a package manager offers SHA-3 integrity
reason: The package managers and registries define the integrity format; none offers SHA-3.
what: Package lockfiles (bun.lock, deno.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml) record SHA-2 integrity hashes, not SHA3-512.

fix: none: changing it would break U1
reason: Ids are immutable once minted (ruling U1); changing the hash would remint every id. The hash derives ids and protects no secret.
what: UUIDv8 identifiers (ADR-008) are derived with SHA-256, not SHA3-512.

fix: none until a hybrid WireGuard handshake ships
reason: WireGuard has no cipher negotiation; its suite cannot be changed.
what: WireGuard tunnels use its fixed Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and BLAKE2s suite, with a pre-shared key as the post-quantum hedge.

fix: measure handshakes per service and drop the fallback groups once none negotiate them
reason: Clients that offer no post-quantum group cannot negotiate otherwise. Support exists in current clients, so the fallback can go.
what: tls.groups lists X25519 and secp256r1 after X25519MLKEM768 for clients without a hybrid group.

fix: per zone: (1) list every proxied record and every Cloudflare edge service on it (proxy, WAF, CDN, Load Balancing, Spectrum); (2) pre-signed DNSSEC with Cloudflare as secondary serves every record DNS-only and drops Secondary DNS Overrides, and Cloudflare Secondary DNS is Enterprise-only, while live or multi-signer signing keeps the proxy but signs with algorithm 13; (3) so migrate a zone to a self-hosted BIND 9 primary signing with algorithm 16 only once each proxied record has moved to a partial (CNAME) setup on a separate zone, or its origin is confirmed to accept direct client traffic, or the owner accepts losing that edge service; (4) publish the algorithm 16 DS at the registrar. A zone that cannot meet (3) keeps this row and is reported to the owner
reason: Cloudflare DNS signs with algorithm 13 only. Ed448 is supported by BIND 9 and by resolvers, so this is hosting work.
what: Every estate DNS zone is treated as Cloudflare-hosted (owner ruling 2026-11-27, "All on Cloudflare") and signs with ECDSA P-256 (algorithm 13), not Ed448 (16).

fix: change opsm and cerro-torre / cerro-sign to sign and verify with Ed448 + ML-DSA-87, carry the new signer into the Trustfile deed that replaces the exemplar Trustfile.a2ml, then remove this row
reason: opsm and cerro-sign signing and verifying must move to Ed448. Support exists in the libraries; this is tool work. The exemplar is legacy A2ML and is not edited; its successor deed carries the new signer.
what: opsm signs packages and releases with hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-87, and the exemplar Trustfile (.machine_readable/contractiles/trust/Trustfile.a2ml, signing) configures Ed25519 per-service release keys for cerro-torre / cerro-sign; neither uses Ed448 + ML-DSA-87.

fix: raise each deployed endpoint (Nginx, Caddy, edge) to TLS 1.3 only, then remove this row
reason: The policy now requires TLS 1.3 only (standards#1715), but deployed endpoints still accept TLS 1.2 until each is reconfigured. TLS 1.3 is supported by every current client.
what: Deployed estate endpoints may still accept TLS 1.2; the policy is TLS 1.3 only.

fix: replace Cloudflare Universal SSL with an ECDSA-only advanced or custom certificate on each zone (the exemplar Trustfile.a2ml sets universal_ssl: true), then remove this row
reason: Cloudflare Universal SSL issues both RSA and ECDSA edge certificates; an ECDSA-only certificate needs an advanced or custom certificate order. This is configuration work.
what: Cloudflare-hosted zones on Universal SSL serve an RSA edge certificate beside the ECDSA one, against the policy rule of ECDSA P-256 only (no RSA).

fix: none until an ML-DSA (or other post-quantum) DNSSEC algorithm is standardised and validating resolvers support it
reason: No post-quantum DNSSEC algorithm is standardised or deployed (TRUST-DEFAULTS-POLICY.adoc). Moving a zone to Ed448 removes trust-defaults-dnssec-ed448 but not this row.
what: DNSSEC signatures carry no ML-DSA-87 component; a signed zone uses Ed448 (algorithm 16) alone where it can, not the Ed448 + ML-DSA-87 hybrid.

fix: none until a TLS 1.3 cipher suite with a SHA-3 hash is standardised and deployed
reason: RFC 8446 fixes the transcript hash and HKDF hash per cipher suite, and every registered TLS 1.3 suite names SHA-256 or SHA-384; there is no SHA-3 suite.
what: TLS 1.3 uses its cipher suite's SHA-2 hash for the handshake transcript and HKDF: SHA-384 for TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, SHA-256 for TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (the last is not offered where configurable), not SHA3-512.

fix: inventory each SHA-256 mandate in standards specifications (tracking issue); for each, either move it to SHA3-512 with a format or version bump that keeps old receipts and digests readable, or give it its own permanent row where an external consumer or format fixes the hash; then remove this row
reason: Specifications written before the 2026-11-27 rulings mandate SHA-256 digests for integrity (for example PROOF-POLICY.adoc :inputs-sha256 receipts and the AXEL policy_hash_sha256). Changing each is a format change with existing records and consumers to migrate.
what: SHA-256 integrity digests mandated by existing standards specifications, not SHA3-512.
